speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office; I see you have a skin lesion on your chest. How long has this spot been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or shape? Also, have you experienced any bleeding, itching, or pain in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful. Given your age and the lesion's growth, has this spot been exposed to the sun frequently, and do you recall if it appeared after any recent trauma or insect bite? Also, have you noticed any new lumps in your neck or armpit area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the chest.

Given your age, diabetes, and the lesion's recent growth without pain or itching, I strongly suspect a non-melanoma skin cancer. I recommend a biopsy for confirmation; please see a dermatologist immediately for this procedure.
